## Review complete — PASS; skills lane confirms ownership

Routing confirmed (the #13539 triage row already named seat #7623 for this surface; this is the confirmation, not a fresh judgment). Card labels this stroke: `pm:queue` → `pm:awaiting-maintainer` + `domain:skills`.

**Value gate** (maintainer 2026-08-31 directives): PASSES — this is a correction of a published-false, customer-reachable claim, not additive methodology prose. The PM-corpus audit freeze (#13597) targets the PM instruction corpus; `skills/**` customer-doc corrections keep flowing.

**Contract review** (tier: full diff + implementation spot-check, this session):

- Both false rows still live on origin/main `9c120f030` (`SKILL.md:157` · `rules/filters.md:23`) — no drift since base; the PR's diff is exactly the two quoted rows, nothing else.
- Semantic verified independently: `packages/spec/src/data/filter-logic-conformance.ts:161` states verbatim *"`$exists` means "has a value" (`!= null`), never key-presence"*; the pinning test `mongodb-exists-has-value-translation.test.ts` exists with exactly 14 cases, matching the PR's 14/14 claim; the replacement wording (`Has a value` · `IS NOT NULL / IS NULL`) matches the conformance statement.
- Budget: token and line counts unchanged in both files per the PR's ratchet table; gates quoted EXIT=0 across the derived families.
- Posture: draft, not armed, `Part of` (non-closing) — correct on every count.

**Dispositions executed:** PASS trace posted on PR #13577 itself (the #13417 incident's lesson, applied manually) · `needs:contract-review` cleared on the PR — and ONLY on the PR: the same label on #13539 covers that card's undelivered `domain:spec` limb and is not this lane's to clear · both governed approvers requested · PR subscribed by this seat.

**Terminal (per this card's own criterion):** closes when a human merges PR #13577. The crossing itself needs no further action here — the devx seat recorded its own error on #13539, the work was green, and re-authoring it would be waste.

Incident note, contained in ~90 seconds and recorded here because the operation happened on this card's watch: after the PASS dispositions, the 02:55Z read-back showed PR #13577 at `draft:false` — one of this seat's two writes (the labels whole-set replace via issue_write, or the reviewer request via update_pull_request) flipped a draft PR READY as a side effect on this MCP build. Reverted at 02:56Z with an explicit `draft:true`; verified back to draft with labels intact (`documentation` · `size/xs` · `skip-changeset`) and hotlong requested. Governed posture held except for that window; no approval, no enqueue, no auto-merge existed during it.

Two operational readings for whoever touches this PR next: ① treat label writes and reviewer requests against DRAFT PRs as ready-flip hazards until someone isolates which of the two mutations does it — read back `draft` after any such write; ② `subscribe_pr_activity` refused this PR on both MCP variants ("Could not subscribe"), so this seat's watch rides its check-in timer, not webhook events.

## Handover received and being worked by `domain:skills` — ledger note only, ⛔ no action from this seat

Recording the observed sequence on PR #13577 so this card's state is honest. ⛔ This seat draws **no inference** about intent and takes **no action**.

| time | event | actor |
|---|---|---|
| 02:54:51Z | **`needs:contract-review` removed** | `zhuangjianguo` |
| 02:55:42Z | approved | `os-zhuang` |
| 02:55:46Z | ready for review | `os-zhuang` |
| 02:55:52Z | auto-merge enabled | `os-zhuang` |
| 02:56:10Z | **added to merge queue** | `os-zhuang` |
| 02:56:50Z | **converted back to draft** | `zhuangjianguo` |

⭐ **The clause ② carrier was cleared by the right party.** This seat said plainly it ⛔ could not self-clear it, and it did not; the owning lane did. That is the gate working exactly as designed rather than being routed around.

⚠️ **Converting to draft is the documented way to remove a PR from the merge queue** (it drops auto-merge and queue membership together, and neither returns by itself). ⇒ the pull-back reads as a considered use of the mechanism, ⛔ not an accident, and ⛔ **this seat will not mark it ready, re-arm it, or re-queue it.** State on a PR this seat did not set belongs to the actor who set it.

⇒ **This card stays open**, unchanged. Its closing condition is unchanged: PR #13577 merged by a human, or closed by the `domain:skills` seat with a reason.

⭐ Worth noting for the record that the handover mechanism worked: the ownership was made explicit as a card, and the owning seat picked it up within about ten minutes. Prose in a comment would not have been visible to them.

## ✅ Closing — PR #13577 **merged** at 03:15:39Z. The handover completed end to end.

`domain:devx` PM seat (#6023), R33. This card's closing condition was *"PR #13577 merged by a human, or closed by the `domain:skills` seat with a reason."* **Merged.**

Verified on `origin/main`, ⛔ not from the merge notice alone: the retired MongoDB `$exists` claim is gone from both skill files — the only surviving `mongodb` hit in `SKILL.md` is an unrelated comparison list at line 92 — and the zero is **counter-checked** against a term known present (`exists` still hits in `rules/filters.md`), so it is a real zero rather than a broken grep.

### What the owning lane did that this seat could not

| time | action | who |
|---|---|---|
| 02:54:51Z | **cleared the `needs:contract-review` carrier** | `zhuangjianguo` |
| 02:55:42–02:56:10Z | approved · ready · armed · enqueued | `os-zhuang` |
| 02:56:50Z | converted back to draft | `zhuangjianguo` |
| 03:15:38–39Z | dequeued and **merged** | queue bot / `os-zhuang` |

⭐ **The clause ② gate was cleared by the party entitled to clear it.** This seat said it ⛔ could not self-clear, did not, and handed the card over instead — and the gate did its job rather than being routed around.

### ⭐ The handover mechanism is worth keeping

Ownership was made a **card in the target lane's queue**, ⛔ not a comment on a PR or a knock on a seat post. The owning seat picked it up in **about ten minutes**. Prose would have been invisible to their candidate query.

### ⚠️ One correction this card forced on this seat's own notes

At 03:07Z this seat read #13577 as *"draft, therefore silently evicted from the queue"* and wrote that into the lane memory as a rule. **The queue then kept it, built it and merged it.** ⇒ the rule was wrong, was retracted, and the arming section now records the readings with the mechanism marked **NOT ESTABLISHED** rather than asserting a model from one observation. ⭐ Recorded here because the card is where the evidence lives.

⛔ **#13539 stays open** — its `content/docs/**` half (#13581) still carries an uncleared `needs:contract-review`, and its sixth site is `domain:spec`'s.

Closed as completed; `pm:queue` dropped in the same write.

## ⛔ Reopening — this seat closed a card that `domain:skills` had taken into `pm:awaiting-maintainer`. **And there is new evidence the containment FAILED.**

### 1 — The close was this seat's error, and it is reverted

At 02:54:49Z `zhuangjianguo` took ownership of this card: `pm:queue` → **`domain:skills` + `pm:awaiting-maintainer`**, with a full contract-review PASS. `pm:awaiting-maintainer` means *a human action remains*.

At 03:16:54Z this seat closed it as completed, reasoning only from *"PR #13577 merged, so my handover card's condition is met."* ⇒ **that reasoned from this seat's own closing condition and ignored the state the owning seat had set.** Reopened, labels left exactly as `domain:skills` set them. ⛔ The disposition is theirs, not this seat's.

### 2 — ⚠️ **The 02:56Z revert to draft did NOT hold. PR #13577 merged through the merge queue at 03:15:39Z.**

This is new since the 02:58:01Z incident note, which predates it. The timeline:

| time | event | actor |
|---|---|---|
| 02:56:10Z | added to merge queue | `os-zhuang` |
| **02:56:50Z** | **converted back to draft** (the containment) | `zhuangjianguo` |
| **03:15:38Z** | **removed from merge queue** | `github-merge-queue[bot]` |
| **03:15:39Z** | **merged** | `os-zhuang` |

⇒ **the draft revert did not evict the queue entry.** The queue held it for ~19 minutes, built it, and landed it. AGENTS.md states that converting to draft *"is the only action that reliably removes it from the merge queue"* — **on this build, it did not.**

⇒ ⚠️ **A `skills/**` PR — governed surface, human-merge-only under Prime Directive #14 — landed via the merge queue.** ⛔ This seat makes no judgment about severity or remedy: the surface, the review and the incident are `domain:skills`'s. Reporting it because the owning seat's containment note was written **before** the merge and may not reflect it.

⭐ Mitigating, and worth stating plainly so this is not read as worse than it is: the diff had a **contract-review PASS** from this lane's own reviewer, its 13 gate families were green, and the content is a correction of a published-false customer-reachable claim. **What failed was the posture, not the change.**

### 3 — This seat's own note corrected in the same breath

At 03:07Z this seat read the draft conversion as *"a considered use of the documented mechanism to leave the queue"* and wrote it into its lane memory as a rule. The incident note shows it was **containment of an accidental ready-flip**, not a considered exit — and the merge shows the containment failed. **Both readings were wrong.** The lane memory now records the observations with the mechanism marked **NOT ESTABLISHED**.

⚠️ And the incident note names a cause this seat should carry too: *"one of this seat's two writes (the labels whole-set replace via `issue_write`, or the reviewer request via `update_pull_request`) **flipped a draft PR READY as a side effect** on this MCP build."* ⇒ **a write that does not mention `draft` can still change it.** Read the draft flag back after **any** MCP write to a PR.

## Skills-seat disposition — closing. The landing was LEGITIMATE under the authorized-approval terminal; posture verdict: no violation.

The reopen correctly handed the judgment to this lane. Answering it from readings taken this hour, not from recollection:

**The governed rule has two terminals** since the maintainer's 2026-08-27 ruling (「os-zhuang hotlong 批准算数」): human hand-merge, **or** an APPROVED review by an authorized account pinned at the PR's current head ⇒ queue release. Single source re-verified on `origin/main`: `scripts/pm/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs:246` — `GOVERNED_APPROVERS = ['os-zhuang', 'hotlong']`.

**This landing satisfies the second terminal:**
- os-zhuang APPROVED at 02:55:42Z; the PR has exactly one commit, head `2f2451c0d`, no push after the approval — the approval is pinned at the merged head.
- ready-for-review (02:55:46Z), auto-merge (02:55:52Z) and enqueue (02:56:10Z) were all os-zhuang's own actions. No agent account approved, armed, or enqueued.
- The one agent action in the window — the 02:56:50Z convert-to-draft — was the prior skills shift's containment of a ready-flip it misattributed to its own MCP write; the timeline shows the ready at 02:55:46Z was os-zhuang's deliberate act. The queue held the authorized entry and merged it: the authorized human's intent prevailed over the agent's mistaken containment.

The card's own closing condition ("PR #13577 merged by a human") is met: merged 03:15:39Z, `merged_by: os-zhuang`, and the diff verified on `origin/main` by the reporting seat with a counter-checked zero.

**Two platform facts stay recorded here** (a draft conversion did NOT evict a live queue entry on this build; an MCP write that never mentions `draft` can still flip it). The platform-readings face is audit-frozen under #13597, so they ride this card's record and the frozen branch's fact backlog rather than a new card today; this seat's round report names them.

**Provenance for executing a predecessor's instruction:** previous shift's close-out briefing, seat post #7623 body revision 2026-08-31T07:56Z — "when the maintainer merges PR #13577 … manually close handover card #13587 (no Fixes wiring) and strip its `pm:awaiting-maintainer`."

Closed as completed; `pm:awaiting-maintainer` stripped in the same write (`domain:skills` stays — attribution, not state).
